title: Shutdown is clean and a rerun resumes rather than restarting
statement: Stopping the supervisor leaves no child process, no bound port and no temporary file from that invocation; rerunning resumes the recorded session and the current stage, and the setup phase changes no bytes. One of the runs is a real interactive session on Windows and Node 24 quit immediately after a completed tool call: it exits cleanly through the supervisor, its process exit status and the supervisor's shutdown record are retained, and it leaves no child, no bound port and no temporary file of that invocation behind.
notes: ⚠️ THE IMMEDIATE-QUIT RUN EXISTS BECAUSE OF F82 (2026-09-12), AND IT IS THE ONE CELL NOTHING ELSE CAN OBSERVE. WHAT WAS MEASURED: over 98 runs against the pinned runtime on Windows, `--mode rpc` on Node 24.18.0 aborts with a libuv assertion - `Assertion failed: !(handle->flags & UV_HANDLE_CLOSING), file src\win\async.c, line 94`, exit 3221226505 (0xC0000409) - when shutdown begins within 50ms of a SECOND OR LATER turn settling. WHAT WAS NOT THE CAUSE: it is not tool execution. A tool call forces a second provider request, and two text-only turns abort identically; one turn never does. Forcing a fresh connection per request and disabling session persistence each still abort. THE CONTROLS WERE CLEAN: Node 22.23.2 in every configuration, print mode with and without a tool call, terminating the child rather than asking it to stop, and every shutdown delayed 50ms or more. WHY IT IS NOT A TASK: Kiln's launch never passes `--mode`, so production runs interactive or, without a TTY, print - and print was clean. No Kiln code is on that stack, and no delay, flag or dependency patch is justified by evidence that does not reach production. THE INTERACTIVE PATH, OBSERVED 2026-09-25 (EVD-0151). It ends in the same `process.exit(0)` as RPC, with an awaited terminal drain in front of it. It was observed in Windows Terminal on Node 24.18.0, where Pi had a real console on both ends and ran interactive: a second turn completed a tool call, and `/quit` was submitted 9 ms and 44 ms after Pi's own `agent_end`, inside the 50 ms window. The keystrokes were synthetic input events sent to a Windows Terminal window verified to be in the foreground, not a physical keypress, and a person reviewed the retained records against their hashes. Both runs exited 0 through the supervisor with a complete shutdown, no surviving tree, no bound port and no run file left. IF IT FAILS: a dedicated defect and an upstream report are opened before this criterion is accepted. A delay is a diagnostic control and is not a fix. ✅ PASS 2026-09-25 on EVD-0151 (the immediate quit after a completed tool call on a second turn, Windows and Node 24) and EVD-0145 (clean shutdown, exact resume and unchanged setup in the documented journey). EVD-0150 is linked as the earlier first-turn runs, which did not meet the second-turn condition. LIMIT: the keys were synthetic input in a verified foreground Windows Terminal window; no physical keypress is claimed.
